$description: Investment Roadmap — the most important table in Progmune. Connects Blind Benchmark → Asset Library → ROI. Answers: what should we build next, what will it cost, what will we gain?
data_source: 5-project blind benchmark (blog, chat, ecommerce, forum, todo)

three_dimensional_gap_model.description: Every FN is classified by which layer it fails at: Asset (do we have a rule?), Detector (can we find it?), Evidence (can we recognize the pattern?)

layers.asset: Does Progmune have a Verification Asset for this protocol category?
layers.detector: Given an Asset exists, can the detector find violations of it in code?
layers.evidence: Given an Asset and a working detector, do we have enough examples to recognize the pattern?

asset_missing.description: No Asset exists for this protocol category

detector_missing.description: Asset exists but detector can't find it (interprocedural gap)

evidence_missing.description: Asset exists, pattern known, but evidence insufficient for reliable detection

capability_status_matrix.description: Per-capability status across all 3 dimensions. ✅ = covered, ⚠️ = partial, ❌ = missing.

capabilities.rationale: 5 Critical FNs. Pattern is well-known (bcrypt/argon2 vs SHA256/MD5). Low implementation effort. Highest ROI.
6 Critical FNs. Highest recall gain. Requires Asset definition + interprocedural check. Medium effort but high impact.
3 Critical FNs. TLS Asset already exists (91% confidence). Just needs extension to detect http vs https. 1 day effort. Do this first.
4 High FNs. Pattern is clear: check_exists before create_reference. Moderate effort.
4 High FNs. Pattern: sanitize → validate_type → validate_range. More complex due to varied validation types.
Only 2 Medium FNs. 1 month effort. Low ROI. Do NOT do this first — let the Asset-first approach close the gap. Revisit when recall > 50%.
1 Low FN. Wait until higher-priority Assets are in place.
1 Medium FN. Can be bundled with Password Hashing Asset.

investment_roadmap.description: Prioritized by ROI. Each step independently verifiable via benchmark re-run.

steps.rationale: 2 days. +19pp. Critical risk. Do this second.
1 week. Crosses 50% recall threshold. Major milestone.

deferred.reason: Only 2 FNs. 30 day effort. Low ROI. Revisit when other gaps are closed and recall is above 50%.

investment_roadmap.verification: Re-run bash blind-benchmark/run.sh after each capability is delivered. The numbers must change.

roi_summary.description: Why start with TLS Enforcement and Password Hashing? Data-driven, not intuition.
best_roi_first: Interprocedural:    30 days → +7.7pp   (0.3pp/day) ← Do NOT start here
roi_summary.key_insight: TLS Enforcement gives 38× more recall per day than Interprocedural Analysis. Do the easy, high-impact things first. Let the hard things wait until they're the bottleneck.
